title: Attributing Agent Failures to Their History Needs an Executed Counterfactual: Toward a Reporting Standard
trick: Before saying an agent failed because of something in its history, freeze the executable state, edit only that history, continue the same agent, and first prove the restored state replays the live run.
framing_stripped: Titled 'Toward a Reporting Standard' and asking for 'intervention-verified evidence' and a 'replay certificate matched to the estimand'; it is (a) a position paper that sorts the history-editing experiments other people already run (DoVer, REFLECT, TRACE, Who&When Pro, Causal Agent Replay) into four classes and notes that none measured whether its restored state matched the live run, plus (b) two measurements that are both disclaimed as non-results: an observational carrier census on ActBench that its own pre-registered guard declared non-evaluable (adjusted odds ratio $1.148$ $[0.627, 2.016]$), and a model-free demonstration on AgentCE-Bench that a snapshot whose SHA-256 digest is identical across five restored clones still diverges from the live continuation in 9 of 24 and 20 of 24 states because the process-global random-stream position was never in the snapshot (sec. 3.2, App. B). The eight-arm history-manipulation design that would apply the standard (App. D) 'has never been run'.
method_equations: Setup (sec. 2): a trajectory reaches step $t$ with environment state $s_t$, process state $p_t$ (random streams, open handles; caches derived from the history are recomputed), executable state $x_t = (s_t, p_t)$, and agent-visible history $h_t$. A history manipulation replaces $h_t$ by $h'_t$ 'while holding the frozen state fixed, then continues under the same policy and compares arms'. Three properties are distinct: (i) the fork restores $x_t$, certified by a replay certificate, 'a measured restored-vs-reference agreement rate under a fixed probe policy'; (ii) exact (pathwise) replay: continuations under a deterministic probe policy and coupled exogenous randomness are bitwise identical; (iii) distributional equality: continuations under independent randomness are equal in distribution. 'Pathwise estimands additionally require (ii); distributional ones require replicated continuations against an estimand-matched control.' Holding $s_t$ fixed while editing $h_t$ 'targets a controlled direct effect of what the agent is shown, given the realized world'; the total effect of an error that also changed the world 'needs a fork before the event or a joint history-and-state arm'. Measurement 3.2 (App. B.3, B.6): 24 states $= 6$ domains $\times$ hidden-slot count $\in \{5, 21\}$ $\times$ anchors $\{1/3, 2/3\}$ on the $5 \times 7$ grid, branch budget 8, fixed ground-truth continuation policy, tool-failure rate $r \in \{0.05, 0.20\}$ from the anchor onward; the divergence statistic is the count of states (of 24) whose per-call success/failure sequence differs between two continuations. Rows (Table 4, seeded replication): two fresh runs same seed $0/24$, $0/24$; prefix-rebuilt state $0/24$, $0/24$; byte-identical snapshot restored into a per-state-seeded process $9/24$, $20/24$ (fractions $0.38$, $0.83$ against an independent-sequence plug-in reference $0.45$, $0.84$); runner's fixed seed $18/24$, $24/24$; unseeded process (separate run) $14/24$, $21/24$; snapshot with captured random-stream state $0/24$, $0/24$; five seeded clones disagreeing among themselves $0/24$, $0/24$; final-grader divergence in any arm $0/24$, $0/24$. Unseeded naive five-clone disagreement (Table 3) $17/24$ and $22/24$, against a post-hoc plug-in expectation for five independent draw sequences of $0.73$ and $0.98$ ($17.4$ and $23.6$ of 24). Measurement 3.1 (App. A, Table 1): share of the 9,199 attack-positive trajectories carried by service responses $0.8490$ $[0.8008, 0.8940]$, against $225/266 = 84.6\%$ of labeled task pairs being service-carried by construction; logistic carrier contrast with fixed effects for 15 risk-behaviour classes and attack method, adjusted odds ratio $1.1484$ $[0.6275, 2.0160]$; first-exposure recovery $13{,}048/13{,}500 = 96.65\%$ (service) against $1{,}705/2{,}460 = 69.31\%$ (local), the latter below the pre-outcome floor of $70\%$ by 17 trajectories. Proposed design (App. D, never run): eight history arms at a frozen state with assistant-side text the only difference; estimands as risk differences of exact continuation success: length tax $L = p_{\mathrm{short}} - p_{\mathrm{clean\text{-}long}}$ (arms 1 vs 2); error content $\Delta_{\mathrm{err}}(d) = p_{\mathrm{healed}}(d) - p_{\mathrm{own}}(d)$, $d \in \{\mathrm{early}, \mathrm{late}\}$ (3 vs 4); provenance $\Delta_{\mathrm{prov}} = p_{\mathrm{byte\text{-}self}} - p_{\mathrm{byte\text{-}foreign}}$ (7 vs 8, same bytes, different source role); and the share $$S = \frac{\Delta_{\mathrm{err}}(\mathrm{late}) - \Delta_{\mathrm{err}}(\mathrm{early})}{p_{\mathrm{own}}(\mathrm{early}) - p_{\mathrm{own}}(\mathrm{late})},$$ with $p_{\cdot}$ the exact-success rate of the named arm. Power sketch: with $p \approx 0.4$–$0.6$, within-task intraclass correlation $\approx 0.2$, $n_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 400$–$550$ effective pairs, the arm-difference standard error is $\approx \sqrt{2p(1-p)/n_{\mathrm{eff}}} \approx 3.0$–$3.5$ points and the minimum detectable effect at 80% power, two-sided $\alpha = 0.05$, is $(1.96 + 0.84)\,\mathrm{SE} \approx 8$–$10$ points; the $\pm 5$-point equivalence margins need $n_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 1{,}500$. State admission rule (App. D.2): five restored clones give identical state hashes and grader outcomes AND an unedited-history restored continuation matches a separately executed live or prefix-rebuilt reference 'with the pathwise rate or distributional margin fixed in advance'.
load_bearing_assumption: That a replay certificate measured under a fixed probe policy with no model in the loop says something about a model-driven continuation forked from the same snapshot. The paper measures (i) and (ii) only for a scripted retry policy on AgentCE-Bench and says so: 'whether realization-level infidelity moves model-driven behavior is unmeasured' (sec. 3.2), and capturing the stream 'does not show the executable state is complete'. If a model's continuation is insensitive to the realization of tool failures (the final grader never diverged, 0/24 in every condition), the certificate is a formality; if it is sensitive, nothing in the paper measures by how much. Second, that the counterfactual norm is attainable where it matters: 'For hosted models the pathwise route may be unavailable' (sec. 5), and the one hosted path tried reproduced 0 of 4 byte-identical resends (App. B.7), so for frontier agents the standard collapses to the distributional route, whose adequate margin the paper never states.
weakest_component: A standard with no instance of itself: 'Neither applies the standard; amendments are disclosed' (sec. 3), 'Neither measurement establishes a behavioral result' (sec. 4), and the one design that would (App. D) 'has never been run' and 'as sized, the design is powered for the sign of the primary contrasts, not for the margins'. The replay evidence is 24 factorial cells, 'not a random sample of the census, so no population coverage is claimed' (Table 3 caption), on one lightweight benchmark with the authors' own snapshot layer and a single scripted policy; the certificate is 'probe-specific' by the paper's own definition, so a pass for the retry policy certifies nothing for a model. The literature census that motivates the norm was coded from 'our own secondhand summaries, no PDFs', with Cohen's $\kappa = 0.66$ on the manipulation question and all nine disagreements one-sided. Pre-registration drift is admitted in print: two arms of the seeded replication 'were added by dated amendment after the fixed-seed results had been seen' and 'the per-state arms were designated primary after both result sets were known'; the TRACE byte-identity criterion was amended 'on a rationale later found mistaken'. The carrier measurement is a pre-declared non-result (floor missed by 17 trajectories) that occupies a third of the appendix.
regime: No model in the loop for the replay result: AgentCE-Bench (rev. 22ae16b7) under the authors' own snapshot layer, fixed ground-truth continuation policy with at most 10 attempts per slot, 24 factorial-cell states (6 domains x hidden slots {5, 21} x anchors {1/3, 2/3}, $5 \times 7$ grid, branch budget 8), tool-failure rates 0.05 and 0.20, census of 144 verdicts over 108 states plus 17 model-generated states with the channel off (App. B.1-B.6). Second environment: AppWorld 0.1.3.post1, reset probe 10 tasks x 5 initialisations (0/10 mismatched) and replay probe 5 tasks with a scripted one-write prefix and full per-application SQLite snapshot (0/5 mismatched) (App. B.5). Hosted-provider probe: $\tau^2$-bench, third-party-served model behind a proxy at temperature 1.0 with best-effort seed, 0 of 4 comparable call pairs reproduced; the authors' own serving path 34/34 calls and 2/2 episodes bitwise (App. B.7). Carrier measurement: ActBench, 300 task pairs, 24,000 trajectories over 20 model-harness configurations (15 models, 6 harnesses, not a full cross), 266/300 pairs labeled, 15,960 labeled attack trajectories, 9,199 attack-positive (App. A). TRACE re-run: 590 compaction boundaries, 4,641 paired PRE/POST rollouts, 20,133 steps, 147 AppWorld tasks, read-only (App. C). Literature census: 200 index cards, 41 past Stage 1, two LLM coders (App. E). Proposed design (not run): 288 paired states in 144 tasks at 3 repetitions per arm on the powered lane, two 36-48-state replication surfaces, two hosted frontier models, minimum detectable effect 8-10 points (App. D.4). Compute and dollar cost: unknown (not in text). Venue: IAB workshop at NeurIPS 2026, non-archival, 20 pages; Salesforce AI Research.
information_asymmetry: (1) Transcript vs executable state. The label a judge writes after the run ('History Error Accumulation', 'unsourced entry followed') exists in hindsight over the completed transcript; the quantity it names, the controlled direct effect of $h_t$ on the continuation given the realized world $s_t$, exists only at run time at the executable state $x_t = (s_t, p_t)$, which is gone unless checkpointed. 'A label assigned by reading a completed transcript, blinded or not, cannot distinguish a cause of failure from something that co-occurs with it' (sec. 1). This is the pipeline's checklist line of 2026-10-25 ('a presence label is not a cause', from C-W43-23 and the killed CL-W43-05) stated as a field norm with four named manipulation classes; CL-W44-06's census probe C-W44-11 ('followed from an unsourced entry' with the full-history pair as control) is still, in this paper's terms, a transcript label on a paired observational cell, and its intervention twins C-W44-12 (delete the unsourced entries at matched tokens: class 1 healed history plus class 3 length match) and C-W44-18 (plant one bullet at a compaction boundary in the SJC harness: class 4 counterfactual injection, 'a controlled error, stale value, or compaction summary inserted where none occurred') are the forms the standard asks for. The ordering the pipeline adopted on 2026-10-30 (kill search, then design) gets a second argument: the census is descriptive and the deletion and injection arms carry the claim. (2) Snapshot content vs process position. The snapshot has the serialized state and its SHA-256 digest; what it does not have is where the process-global random stream stands, and that lives only in the live process: 'no snapshot field records the stream's position' (sec. 3.2). Five clones restored from one digest 'agreed with one another in 24 of 24 states while differing from the live continuation in 9 and 20 of 24' (abstract). For same-snapshot replay probes this is exact: a within-fork contrast (summary arm vs full-history arm continued from one restored state) is internally valid, but 'the live-vs-restored control ties that instance to the observed trajectory' (sec. 2), and that control is the one the pipeline's probe designs do not have. C-W44-18 forks the agent at a compaction boundary inside the SJC/ACON harness on AppWorld; TRACE forks there by prefix re-execution under a recipe hash and 'Whether the 590 reached states were identical was measured neither by the authors nor by us' (App. C.4); the paper's own AppWorld probe found that 'a file-copy restore was silently ignored, with no error raised' until cached in-memory database engines were reset (App. B.5). So the probe design owes one row before any arm is scored: an unedited-history continuation from the restored boundary against the live (or prefix-rebuilt) continuation, under the same policy, seed and provider, with its agreement rate or margin fixed in advance; clone agreement is 'insufficient' (App. D.2). (3) Outcome vs realization. The grader saw nothing: 'final-grader divergence under the oracle retry policy was 0/24 in every condition: an outcome-only metric would have hidden the problem' (sec. 3.2). Pass-rate probes (C-W43-08's Pass3, C-W44-12's all-criteria pass rate) read only the outcome; the paper's open cell, and the one measurement no one holds, is a replay certificate with a model in the loop: fork a frontier agent $k$ times from one restored boundary with and without the captured stream position, and measure how far the per-call action sequence and the outcome move: 'whether realization-level infidelity moves model-driven behavior is unmeasured' (sec. 3.2). That is a one-GPU-week-or-less, API-only probe on a public harness, and it decides whether every same-snapshot compaction probe in L4 needs the stream capture or can ignore it. (4) Pathwise vs distributional, by who serves the model. The coupled-randomness certificate exists only where the serving path is controlled (34/34 calls bitwise on the authors' path, 0/4 on a hosted path, App. B.7). Every probe under CL-W44-06 runs hosted frontier receivers at temperature 0 (HSC-Bench receivers, GPT-5.6 Luna in C-W43-08), so the pathwise route is closed and the estimand is distributional: the three repeats per cell are the certificate, and the paper's rule is that they be reported 'against an unedited-history live-vs-restored control' with a 'prespecified margin on a named metric' (sec. 5). The pipeline's own W41 finding (temperature-0 variance is the serving stack's arithmetic) is the same fact from the other side. (5) Concentration vs construction. The ActBench census shows a headline share, $84.9\%$ of unsafe actions carried by service responses, that 'tracks task-pair allocation by construction' ($225/266 = 84.6\%$) and vanishes under adjustment (odds ratio $1.148$, interval crossing 1). SJC's '83% of failed runs trace back to an action that carries out a specific summary entry' (the current belief CL-W44-06 argues against) is a share whose denominator is the summaries' own composition; the per-class recovery floor the paper adds ($70\%$; local carriers recovered at $69.31\%$) is a check the pipeline's typed matcher has no analogue for yet: how often the labeler locates the entry at all, per class, before the shares are compared.
occupies: The named position, now in print at a NeurIPS 2026 workshop, that any 'the agent failed because of X in its history' claim needs a per-instance executed counterfactual from a frozen executable state or a validated estimator, with a reported replay certificate matched to the estimand (pathwise or distributional) and an unedited-history live-vs-restored control; the four-class taxonomy of history manipulations (healed history, provenance swap, length-matched placebo, counterfactual injection) with its precedent map; the result that a hash-identical, five-clone-certified snapshot diverges from the live run in 9/24 and 20/24 states (per-state seeds; 18/24 and 24/24 under one fixed seed) because the random-stream position was omitted, and that capturing it gives 0/24; the finding that TRACE's recipe hash is not a measured certificate; the ActBench carrier non-result; and the eight-arm paired design with its estimands $L$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{err}}$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{prov}}$, $S$ and power sketch. It does not claim, and leaves open, any behavioural result (both measurements disclaimed), a model-in-the-loop replay certificate, the adequate distributional margin for hosted models, and the design itself, which is proposed and unrun.

neighbors.title: Towards Reliable Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents: An Empirical Study of Execution Instability (TRACE)
neighbors.trick: At each of 590 AppWorld compaction boundaries, rebuild the state by re-executing the recorded code prefix, then continue twice, once under a less-compacted control and once under the new summary, and score the paired continuations; the paper calls it 'the closest executable-surface precedent' and faults it for checking a hash of the recipe, not of the reached state, so 'its pairing is unverified'.

neighbors.title: Who&When Pro: Can LLMs Really Attribute Failures in AI Agents?
neighbors.trick: Replay a successful prefix exactly, inject one error after it, and so manufacture 12,326 failed trajectories with golden step labels; the paper credits it with executing rather than inferring, and notes it reports no measured replay certificate and that its own evaluators still attribute from transcripts.

neighbors.title: Causal Agent Replay: Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures
neighbors.trick: Treat a run as a structural causal model, apply a do-operation at one step, hold the recorded actions before it fixed, re-run forward under the same stochastic policy and report the shift in the outcome distribution with intervals; the paper calls it the method 'closest to the reporting norm' and says it 'validates only on two synthetic causal models and reports no numeric action-match rate or live-vs-restored baseline'.

neighbors.title: REFLECT: Intervention-Supported Error Attribution for Silent Failures in LLM Agent Traces
neighbors.trick: Diagnose a suspect step, inject a repair message into the recorded conversation state, re-run at temperature 0 (placebo and wrong-step controls at 0.2) and use the verified outcome flip to refine the attribution; the paper notes it 'reports no replay-fidelity measurement and does not state how the rollback state is restored'.

neighbors.title: The Long-Horizon Task Mirage? Diagnosing Where and Why Agentic Systems Break (HORIZON)
neighbors.trick: Collect 3,100+ long-horizon trajectories across four domains and attribute failures with a seven-category LLM-judge taxonomy validated against human annotation; the paper's example of the correlational trap, since it 'never resumes from an intermediate state, so its "History Error Accumulation" label is post-hoc'.

theme_fit.why: a reporting standard for attributing an outcome to who moved (history, environment state, process randomness, serving path), a measured instance of a certificate that passes and is wrong, and the carrier census as a benchmark-validity lesson: the lane's attribution and validity questions directly

the compaction summary is the paper's own class-4 manipulation and TRACE its closest precedent; it supplies the control (unedited-history live-vs-restored) that CL-W44-06's same-snapshot probes lack, not a compaction result

sandbox checkpoint/restore (DeltaBox cited), snapshot digests and process state are the systems substrate, but the paper measures replay fidelity on a lightweight benchmark and builds no serving or rollout machinery

limitation_quotes: Neither applies the standard; amendments are disclosed (§4, Appendices A–C). (sec. 3)
Neither measurement establishes a behavioral result: Measurement 3.1 was declared non-evaluable (§3.1) and Measurement 3.2 is model-free. (sec. 4)

First, final-grader divergence under the oracle retry policy was 0/24 in every condition: an outcome-only metric would have hidden the problem, and whether realization-level infidelity moves model-driven behavior is unmeasured. (sec. 3.2)

Capturing it yields exact replay for this probe by coupling the exogenous randomness across clones (common random numbers [15]; record-and-replay [22]); it does not show the executable state is complete. (sec. 3.2)
For hosted models the pathwise route may be unavailable [1, 33, 23], as on the one path we tried (Appendix B); a paired-contrast design is in Appendix D (proposed, not run). (sec. 5)
The design proposed in the second agenda item has never been run: every quantity below is a design parameter, not a result. (App. D)
as sized, the design is powered for the sign of the primary contrasts, not for the margins. (App. D.4)

Whether the 590 reached states were identical was measured neither by the authors nor by us: TRACE is the closest executable-surface precedent, and it reports no measured replay certificate, so its pairing is unverified. (App. C.4)

Both read only our own secondhand summaries, no PDFs, so the codes describe the cards, not the papers, and can err in both directions (sparse cards create false negatives, misreadings false positives); silence was coded as silence. (App. E)
Our census excluded position papers without coded failure data, so it cannot show the norm is unproposed. (sec. 2)
The sample is small, and non-reproduction is localized to the hosted path; we cannot localize it further within that path. (App. B.7)

Two arms were added by dated amendment after the fixed-seed results had been seen: the five-clone seeded arm, to test the clone-agreement consequence that result suggested, and the per-state-seed repeat, because one process seed makes the six domains of a cell share a single live realization (four distinct realizations across the 24 states). No acceptance criterion changed; the per-state arms were designated primary after both result sets were known (App. B.6)
limitations_as_complaints: I cannot get the pathwise certificate on the models I actually run: on the hosted path 'three request payloads were each re-sent byte-identically with the same seed (four comparable call pairs across the three), and none reproduced its completion (0 of 4)' while the authors' own serving path did 34/34 (App. B.7), and 'For hosted models the pathwise route may be unavailable' (sec. 5); so my frozen-state fork needs replicated continuations against an unedited-history control with a 'prespecified margin on a named metric', and the paper never says what margin is adequate or how many repeats buy it.

My snapshot passes every check I own and is still not the live run: five clones from one digest agreed '24 of 24' and 'differing from the live continuation in 9 and 20 of 24' (abstract), the cause being a random-stream position 'no snapshot field records' (sec. 3.2); the final grader hid it ('0/24 in every condition'), and 'whether realization-level infidelity moves model-driven behavior is unmeasured' (sec. 3.2), so I do not know whether a model forked from my compaction boundary is sensitive to it.

The standard has never been exercised on an agent end to end: 'The design proposed in the second agenda item has never been run' (App. D); with 288 paired states at three repetitions the minimum detectable effect is '8–10 points' and the 5-point equivalence margins 'require either $n_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 1{,}500$ effective pairs or a pilot-estimated within-state covariance' (App. D.4), so a history-attribution result at the sizes compaction papers run (hundreds of boundaries) is powered for sign only.

history.note: W45 weekly run; evidence_level full-text (arxiv.org/html/2611.05650v1, LaTeXML, 5 sections plus appendices A-F, read in full; abstract and metadata via export.arxiv.org API; five neighbour abstracts via one API id_list call); lane context L1 primary, L4 secondary: CL-W44-06 (compaction-attributable failures; probes C-W44-11, C-W44-12, C-W44-18, C-W43-08) and the killed CL-W43-05 relied on presence labels, checklist 2026-10-25 'a presence label is not a cause'; information_asymmetry names what the replay certificate and the 9/24, 20/24 snapshot-vs-live divergence mean for the same-snapshot replay probes
